svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS D10 — Chapter 10 · Ch10_TraceSpectral, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 1,515 declarations of the 83 items on C10, each with its kind, file, line and state; 179 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted.

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of C10's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card. First the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: The transpose uses the conjugate isotype in the negative space. The norm weight is applied to the full test space in the diagram. Appendix D's two-sided decay topology uses growing exponential weights in log coordinates. The decaying factors on p. 441 would all be bounded by the zeroth weight.

g.text: This statement concerns derivatives of the test function's Mellin transform. Only orders below the strict cutoff give continuous Sobolev moments at the boundary.

g.text: The proof divides a polar-free entire Mellin transform within the scalar Schwartz–Bergman space and uses the strict Sobolev cutoff at the boundary.

g.text: In place of the finite-band argument on pp. 443 and 446, use bounded Blaschke products on a wider strip. At a boundary zero, the index includes only derivative orders satisfying the strict cutoff 2k + 1 < s (F152).

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The ambient approximation uses strip Blaschke products in place of the finite-band argument on p. 443. The reverse inclusion is the remaining geometric approximation in the strip norm.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The strict boundary inequality is the correction F152. Necessity outside the strip follows by embedding a wider interval with degree zero and applying its endpoint criterion.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: At the boundary the admitted orders satisfy the strict inequality 2k+1<s. The proof uses Mellin division and weighted Sobolev approximation.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The boundary moments use the strict reciprocal-weight cutoff. Mellin division replaces the finite-band argument on pp. 443 and 446.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: At the strip edges the degree satisfies 2k + 1 < s. The reverse inclusion uses Mellin division and approximation in the weighted strip norm.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Finite moment support is dense by the preceding cutoff argument. The reverse common-kernel inclusion then gives density of the single interpolants themselves.

g.text: Density follows from wider-strip Blaschke products and the reverse inclusion of the common kernel in the geometric theta closure (Theorem 10.2.2.1).

g.text: The paper does not state this. The squared norm of a jet of order m is at least a constant times 4 ^ m, and for m ≥ (s - 1) / 2 at least a constant times the logarithm of the inverse distance of its real offset from the edge.

g.text: Assume trace class for all tests. Factor the homogeneous radial profile into finite sums of iterated convolutions of smooth compactly supported functions on ℝ. The approximation-number product inequality then gives arbitrary polynomial decay.

g.text: This records the biorthogonal lift and the norm bounds. The claimed Schauder conclusion fails even for Schauder input in Banach spaces. The caller chooses the tolerance, as in (10.4.2.24). The strict collar and arbitrary index type also cover the finite and empty families of §10.2.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The perturbation conclusion uses biorthogonality and exact quotient lifts, with no general Schauder claim.

text.tspan: · pp. 472–473 · 59 declarations, 10 deviating from the print

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The identity is stated for any quotient vector.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The zero set is restricted to the strip, and its boundary and interior multiplicities are those of §10.2. The directed set consists of finite rectangles.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Convolution acts on the lifted output vector. The printed transposed input factor gives projection after convolution, as in (10.4.3.14). The geometric-output components are assumed Cauchy in the projective topology. Section 10.3 supplies the spectral components after grouping all jets of each zero.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The limit is taken in the ambient space of (10.4.3.43), with convolution on the output factor as required by this operator order. Equation (10.4.3.42) gives a limit in the quotient tensor space.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Clause (2) omits the offset range. Read it on the domain of (10.4.3.38) in clause (3), the boundary and interior of the strip.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Stated for an arbitrary index type, with tails taken over finite sets disjoint from a finite exceptional set.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: For the operator in (10.4.3.45), convolution acts on the orthogonal output lift. The rectangles use injections of the actual strip zeros and the strict §10.2 boundary cutoff.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Both conclusions concern the same ambient rectangles, with convolution on the output and the repaired indexing of §10.4.3.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The ambient tensors use the repaired output action and strip indexing of §10.4.3.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This records a consequence independent of the ambiguous index bounds and tensor type in the display.
